chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from his father, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'If four people testified in my presence against a man for adultery, and among them is a son of the adultery (a bastard), I would apply the legal penalty (hadd) upon them all, because his testimony is not valid, nor can he lead the people (in prayer).'

key_terms.لَحَدَدْتُهُمْ: I would apply the legal penalty (hadd) upon them

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a son of the adultery (walad al-zina) as a witness and prayer leader in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) rules that if a *walad al-zina* (son of fornication) is among the four witnesses, the Imam applies the *hadd* penalty to all four, demonstrating that his testimony is invalid (*mardud*). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the defect of illegitimacy not only disqualifies him from leading prayer (*imamah*) but also renders his witness testimony insufficient for legal penalties, thereby ensuring the integrity of the judicial process.
